title: Find out why the lazy rows walk sometimes cannot find the Background layer
goal: One of the scripted walks that checks the layers list occasionally stops partway through, saying it cannot find the layer it wants to scroll from, and then passes on the next run. Find out whether the walk is asking for something that is not always there yet, or whether the list really does lose a row sometimes.
notes:
Seen once on 2026-09-09 while splitting LayersPanel.swift, in:

  Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build layers

Output:
  layers-lazy-rows-walk  45s  FAILED  step 270 (scrollPanel): nothing called "Background" is in the panel to scroll from; the ones that are: Grid Settings / Tool bar, grid off, Zoom level / Tool bar, Layers section / a dock section header, Rectangle 24 / layer, ... Library section / a dock section header ...

Not reproduced: the same walk passed alone against HEAD before the split (Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/layers-lazy-rows-walk.json, status ok), alone after the split (status ok), and in the same group run again straight afterwards (6 passed, 0 failed). The panel split it was seen during changed no code, only which file each type sits in, so this looks like a pre-existing flake rather than a regression. The listing in the failure has 24 Rectangle rows and no Background row, so the likely story is that the list had not finished mounting rows when step 270 asked.
acceptance: The walk is run at least five times in the same group and the outcome of each run is recorded
Either the cause is named and fixed so five runs in a row pass, or the walk is shown to be asking too early and is made to wait for the row
